contract.intent: Implement and validate the portable AgentsKit Harness package and its CLI.

outOfScope: automatic git push or PR creation

outcomes.statement: The typed harness library builds, exposes a usable CLI lifecycle, and installs correctly in a clean consumer project.
The contract, state machine, evidence, stale detection, and approval protocol are enforced.
The public harness API exposes a typed, dependency-aware plugin lifecycle with deterministic cleanup and contribution isolation.
Every new verification run records an ordered lifecycle event log with a verifiable hash chain bound to the run source and contract; legacy logs are identified explicitly.
The verification result is attested in the lifecycle log and human approval rejects a tampered run projection.
Human approval and tracking authorization decisions are recorded in the lifecycle log with the exact verified digest, source revision, and contract binding.
A terminal run is accepted only when its projection, verification event, human decision event, source, and contract are semantically consistent, through both the public API and status CLI.
An interrupted writer leaves a fail-closed lock that can be inspected and recovered only through explicit human-authorized stale-lock recovery, without deleting live or malformed locks.
A complete run can be exported as a portable Ed25519-signed evidence bundle and independently verified, including the projection, event log, and referenced check outputs.
Signed evidence verification binds a bundle to an explicit key identity and active trust store, and rejects unknown, mismatched, or revoked keys while allowing controlled rotation.
Sensitive tool actions pause before execution and enter the runtime only after an explicit human approval; rejection and unresolved approval remain fail-closed and auditable.
Named verification profiles compose deterministic, validated overlays without changing the kernel guarantees.
Optional context providers expose a typed, provenance-bearing seam suitable for Doc Bridge and Playbook integrations.
The optional Doc Bridge adapter resolves real indexed knowledge into deterministic provenance-bearing context snapshots.
A resolved context snapshot is frozen into the planned run with a reproducible context hash and lifecycle event.
The common CLI protocol can resolve a Doc Bridge snapshot and attach it to a planned run from a portable JSON file.
Imported context snapshots reject tampering when their semantic contents no longer match their cryptographic snapshot hash.
The public CLI and API aggregate reproducible historical run metrics for measuring harness improvement.
The public API records a correlated, privacy-preserving agent session and guarded tool lifecycle during implementation.
Every recorded tool action receives a deterministic allow/block decision before it can enter the pending execution lifecycle.
Allowed tool actions execute through a bounded runtime and produce structured hashed completion or failure evidence.
Allowed actions can execute through a shell-free child-process runtime with timeout, output limits, and structured recovery evidence.
Allowed actions can execute through an optional Docker sandbox with deny-by-default isolation and resource limits.
Terminal tool evidence identifies the actual sandbox image and effective security/resource profile used for each Docker action.
Baseline evidence records preserve a validated SHA-256 digest of the evidence file and reject malformed digests.
The Playbook and package distribution metadata document the portable protocol and contribution workflow.
